title: RAW UNREVIEWED: complete f83r lyric plus instruction under one source-fixed literal writing law
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED. Nominate already-owned full f83r.25–30 P4 and .31–44 P5 as a literal complete Harley978 lyric/instruction pair under one injective variable-width source-letter writer preserving whole-word boundaries. Independently collated lyric words, syllable-to-note underlay and the written red-cross cue are external inputs; the target cannot supply those inputs. This deliberately stronger source-copy hypothesis may fail immediately on word counts and does not reopen GDT970 or claim a music owner.

complete_targets.instruction_nomination: Entire already-owned f83r.31–44 P5, 62 projected ZL groups; fixed allocation, not an observed instruction.

mechanism.law: One finite injective nonempty source-letter-to-target-symbol-string code is used for both complete source texts. Literal source word boundaries map one-to-one to target group boundaries. Same source spelling always yields the same target whole, across the two units; different complete source spellings must remain distinguishable. Source language does not change the code.
alternatives_fixed_before_collation: Complete English lyric as written in Harley978 f11v plus the complete Latin operative instruction text as written.
Complete Latin sacred contrafactum as written in the same folio plus the same complete Latin operative instruction text.
mechanism.source_units: The entire one lyric text and the entire written operative instruction block, not selected lines, modern paraphrases, snippets or a hand-picked seven-rule serializer. No lyrics/instructions interchange or moving stanza boundary after inspection.
mechanism.no_defaults: Neither Latin nor English is assumed to be the Voynich language. These are two explicit source-copy hypotheses. EVA symbols and the 98 learned units are not declared an alphabet; target literal-symbol policy must be frozen separately. Native source contractions remain written forms with an explicit diplomatic reading, not freely expanded after a mismatch.
mechanism.external_music_coupling: The source-fixed underlay assigns source word/syllable occurrences to current-layer note/rest events; the written red cross is between MN009 and MN010. Under one resulting literal reading, the instruction cue must refer to that same source-defined event/lyric location. It cannot be an unrelated freely bound location.

external_inputs_already_owned: Harley978 f11v cached whole-folio source and explicit current-layer 97-event inventory with red-cross marker, operative R01–R07 and retained duration alternatives in ROTA_SOURCE_EVENTS.
Both English lyric and Latin sacred contrafactum are documented as separately written on that source folio. Their existence is not a target music-owner binding.

specific_input_not_yet_collated.needed: Complete diplomatic source-word sequence for each of the two lyrics and the full written Latin instruction block; a source-word/syllable occurrence → current-layer note/rest event tuple including melisma, rests and exact cross location.
specific_input_not_yet_collated.current_gap: ROTA_SOURCE_EVENTS explicitly excludes complete lyric transcription and lyric alignment. No such tuple is asserted to exist in its structured packet. Existing pixels are not opened in this tranche; source exposure is not new admission.
specific_input_not_yet_collated.decision_bearing_use: Before any decoder, compare whole word counts (33 and62 in the projected ZL packet), repeated source-word identities and entire unit boundaries. If both exact-copy alternatives fail, reject this narrow coupling without adding contractions, word aliases, omitted clauses or a new boundary. If a fixed alternative survives, only then consider whether one whole writing law fits both complete units and forces the same lyric/cue identity. This can remove arbitrary locally assigned word values, not just execute their story.

paid_assumptions: Literal copying of this precise medieval source pair is a stronger historical claim than generic music content.
P4 is lyric and P5 is instruction; their paragraph boundaries are prose-layout priors, not known verse boundaries.
Word-boundary preservation and one injective variable-width source-letter code are explicit narrow writing hypotheses, not observed structural facts.
One source layer, diplomatic contraction policy, target literal-symbol policy and source language alternative must be fixed before any fit.
The written instruction must actually determine the cross/entry relation in the same source underlay; independently invented cues are excluded.

unequal_consequences.input: The same independently collated source words and cross/underlay tuple.
unequal_consequences.main: One frozen code explains both whole units; repeated source words and the entry-cue location retain identity in both registers.
unequal_consequences.rival: Instruction-only music prose with free 53 whole-word values may execute every performance rule without reproducing any lyric wording or underlay. It is not a pass of this literal source-copy contract.

unequal_consequences.input: English lyric versus Latin contrafactum with the same melody and instruction.
unequal_consequences.main: The two source alternatives have fixed distinct literal words and word/letter identity constraints.
unequal_consequences.rival: Melody/rhythm agreement alone may leave both possible; no language is selected by the same notes. A word-count or shared-code contradiction can eliminate one/both literal alternatives without changing the score.
